svg.text: Control: where data may go, and what checks it
Everything derived from data (a mask, a value per case, a log line, a trained model) keeps the class of its source.
Class 1: open data (e.g. WMH Challenge)
may go anywhere it is released for: GitHub, the website, the cloud
Class 2: data under a use agreement
may go as far as the institution's model hub (Clé),
never to public places
Class 3: own patient cohorts
stay on the workstation; only the local
model (and Clara) read them
Split every task
reading the images, values per case
and cohort facts: workstation only
code, method, literature and the
write-up without data: may use Clé
paths and structure are not content;
aggregates over a whole cohort only
when no single case can be seen
Five checks, in the order a request meets them
1 Weiche relay: fixed rules per model request
subject ids or cohort names anywhere, a data folder as project, or a tool
call that opens data or images: the local model answers, not Clé
2 Kernel sandbox around Clara (no root)
Landlock: writes only in listed folders; TCP only to three local ports.
seccomp: no UDP (DNS), no ICMP, no raw sockets; strace shows loopback only
3 Approval gate for commands and writes
deny rules, then System One (run only at p >= 0.8, never deny on its own),
otherwise the human decides in the terminal or with a button on the phone
4 Exit guard for outside questions
frag-draussen: rules and a local model check that a literature question
carries no data before it goes to open APIs or a cloud model
5 Publish check before every push
pruefe-veroeffentlichung: every dataset released, no unreleased names,
no home paths, case files only in assigned folders; else no push
Measured: 27 of 27 sandbox checks (29 Oct 2026); the gate let 0 of 36
approval-needed commands through at p >= 0.8 (19 Oct test set);
the publish check passed before each push.
